memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Patient presents with depression, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and allergic rhinitis.
Low mood, fatigue, poor concentration for 4 weeks; polyuria, polydipsia; sneezing, nasal congestion, itchy eyes. BMI 23 kg/m2, BP 128/78, random glucose 162 mg/dL, nasal mucosa pale, lung clear. Smoking status: never smoked (0 pack-years).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
sertraline 50 mg OD
metformin 500 mg BD
cetirizine 10 mg HS
fluticasone nasal spray, one spray each nostril OD
montelukast 10 mg HS

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
PHQ-9 12 (mild depression)
TSH 2.1 µIU/mL (0.4-4.0)
Vitamin B12 340 pg/mL (200-900)
HbA1c 7.8% (4.0-5.6)
Fasting plasma glucose 158 mg/dL (70-99)
Urine albumin‑creatinine ratio 22 mg/g (<30)
Dilated fundus exam: mild microaneurysms, no macular edema
Skin prick test: positive to dust mite, grass pollen
Total serum IgE 210 IU/mL (<100)

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Patient presents with depression, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and allergic rhinitis.
Improved mood, occasional insomnia; polyuria reduced; allergic symptoms controlled on cetirizine. Weight stable, BP 126/76, random glucose 138 mg/dL, nasal mucosa mildly erythematous. Smoking status: never smoked (0 pack-years).

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been feeling better overall, less sad and more energy at work. My sugar readings have been around 130 fasting. My nose still gets a bit stuffy in the evenings but the spray helps. I’m adhering to meds except I missed sertraline twice last week due to travel.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked for 2025-11-15 at 10:30 AM with Dr Suresh Menon (D05) in Pulmonology clinic.

Patient presents with depression, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and allergic rhinitis.
Mood stable, reports occasional missed doses; polyuria resolved; allergic symptoms mild. Weight 68 kg, BP 124/72, random glucose 124 mg/dL, nasal mucosa normal. Smoking status: never smoked (0 pack-years).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Dilated fundus exam (repeat): mild microaneurysms temporally, no macular edema or hard exudates. Visual acuity 6/6 both eyes. Recommend annual screening.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Referral to Endocrinology, Victoria Hospital, for optimisation of diabetes management considering persistent HbA1c >6.5% despite triple oral therapy.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Endocrinology review: patient advised to add empagliflozin 10 mg OD, continue current agents, lifestyle reinforcement. HbA1c target <7%. No hypoglycaemia reported. Follow‑up in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Patient presents with depression, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and allergic rhinitis.
Mood good, medication adherence improved; empagliflozin started 2 months ago, reports weight loss 2 kg, fasting glucose 110 mg/dL. Allergic symptoms well controlled. BP 122/70, nasal mucosa clear. Smoking status: never smoked (0 pack-years).
